transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-07-21
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nandakumar (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (CTO, Brightscale), Maya Patel (ML Engineer), Sam Ortiz (Head of Eng)

Summary (auto-generated): Walkthrough of the Redwood Console focusing on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdown, and action items to onboard Brightscale for a pilot. Customer asked specific questions about cost attribution, VPC deployment, and SSO/KMS.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan Lee from Redwood, AE on the account. With me is Priya our Solutions Engineer.
[00:12] Priya: Hi all, quick agenda — we'll walk the Console, show usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and then go into cost breakdowns and optimization suggestions. Save questions for the end but feel free to interrupt.
[00:23] Alex: Sounds good, thanks. Quick context — Brightscale is running an internal assistant and some document search embeddings; we're exploring moving inference off our infra to reduce ops overhead. Main concerns are cost predictability and data residency.
[00:40] Jordan: Great, that's helpful. Priya, show the Console.
[00:47] Priya: Alright, opening the Console, top-left is the main usage view - you can filter by date range, route, and model. Here you can see request volume, tokens in/out, and latency P95. Notice the per-route breakdown on the right.
[01:10] Priya: For Brightscale you'd create routes for each product surface — e.g., "search-embeddings", "assistant-chat", "summarization" — and those show separate cost lines. You can pin an SLO per route and set alert thresholds.
[01:28] Maya: How granular is cost attribution? We need to show finance team per-feature cost.
[01:34] Priya: We do token-level attribution; the Console maps tokens to routes and models and emits both USD and token counts. There's a cost-per-token mapping per model and you can override pricing rules for Dedicated SKUs.
[01:50] Jordan: Important note — the Console shows both raw per-token cost and amortized cost after batching/caching. So your finance view can compare naive cost vs optimized cost.
[02:05] Alex: Can we export that breakdown? CSV or BI connector?
[02:09] Priya: Yes, export to CSV and we have a BigQuery connector for enterprise customers. You can schedule daily exports.
[02:18] Sam: If we route the assistant to a cheaper quantized model for low-risk flows, does the dashboard show savings?
[02:25] Priya: Yeah, the per-route view includes model variant columns and shows delta if you switch variants. There's also a simulation mode — apply a hypothetical percent of traffic shifted and the Console projects cost impact.
[02:40] Maya: Nice. About caching — you mentioned prefix/KV caching — how visible is cache hit/miss?
[02:46] Priya: We surface cache hit rate per route and per model; also a histogram of sequence lengths which helps tune cache TTLs. Higher cache hit reduces tokens billed, which is reflected in the cost column.
[03:00] Alex: For our compliance team, we need audit logs and key management. If we go Dedicated in our VPC, can we bring our KMS?
[03:10] Jordan: Yes — Private/Dedicated options allow customer-managed KMS and audit logs. We'll include the SOC2 and architecture diagram in the security pack.
[03:20] Maya: And data residency? We're EU-first.
[03:24] Priya: You can pin region and enforce routing policies so EU traffic stays in EU regions. The Console's routing policy UI has a region constraint field.
[03:34] Alex: On latency — our assistant needs <200ms median token latency for interactivity; what SLAs do you guarantee on Dedicated?
[03:43] Jordan: Our Dedicated offering includes SLA-backed latency percentiles; typical median is sub-100ms on N variants for short context. We'll share performance profiles for the model you pick. For hosted, there are best-effort latency numbers.
[03:58] Sam: How do we measure tail latency?
[04:01] Priya: The Console exposes P50/P95/P99 and traces per-request. You can drill into slow requests and see the model variant, token count, and whether a cache miss or cold start occurred. We also surface queue depths and batching sizes.
[04:18] Alex: On pricing — can you show a worked example for our typical monthly volume?
[04:22] Jordan: Sure, we have an example route with 5M tokens/month for assistant-chat. If on hosted with model X, rough cost is $X per 1k tokens; the Console projection shows token cost and an optimization suggestion (enable batching and a medium quant profile) which reduces cost by ~35% in this example.
[04:42] Priya: Also call out that Dedicated commits change unit economics — reserved capacity lowers per-token prices and guarantees throughput.
[04:51] Maya: For a pilot, we'd likely start hosted then move dedicated if numbers make sense.
[04:56] Jordan: Yep — common path. We'll recommend a pilot with a week of benchmarking using your sample traffic; Priya can run a side-by-side to show cost and latency comparisons.
[05:10] Priya: Quick note on Optimize: it gives batching suggestions based on observed payloads. For example, if 60% of your requests are short (<64 tokens) we recommend a batching window that groups them to improve GPU utilization. The Console can apply these changes as suggestions or auto-apply in Dedicated.
[05:30] Sam: What about function/tool calling and streaming billing implications?
[05:34] Priya: Streaming has slightly different billing semantics because of tokens-in vs tokens-out timing, but the Console separates those metrics. For tool calls you can see calls per route and embed them in the cost view.
[05:45] Alex: Any integration with our internal SSO?
[05:48] Jordan: Yes SAML/SSO supported, RBAC roles are configurable in Console. We'll include SSO config docs in the security pack.
[06:00] Maya: We're concerned about transcription errors — if someone from finance reads exported CSVs will they see model names scrambled?
[06:07] Priya: Model names come from our catalog; the Console uses model IDs for exports so mapping stays stable.

[06:15] Jordan: Ok let's recap next steps, I'll send the pricing and dedicated options, Priya will share the benchmark guide and recording, Maya will upload the sample traffic and prompts.
[06:28] Alex: Thanks all, that was helpful.
[06:30] Meeting end
